sentence: A 36-year-old woman with no relevant medical or epidemiological history was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit for sepsis and meningitis due to type B meningococcus isolated in blood and cerebrospinal fluid cultures.

He received fluid therapy support, ceftriaxone and vancomycin for 10 days with disappearance of clinical and analytical parameters of sepsis although with persistence of daily fever of 38° well tolerated in the afternoon, with no other infectious focality in complementary tests that included: serial blood cultures, urine culture, chest x-ray , abdominal ultrasound and head CT.

She enters the internal medicine ward to complete the study and evolution; She remains hemodynamically stable and in good general condition, with fever up to 38.5oC well tolerated, right subclavian central venous access with no evidence of infection, few petechiae in the lower extremities in the regression phase, and the rest of the general and neurological examination being normal.

The blood count, hemostasis, renal, hepatic, thyroid and lipid profile were normal, highlighting a ferritin value of 775 µg/dl, ESR 90 mm1 hour, CRP at 23.8 mg/dl (VN <0.3 mg /dl) and procalcitonin at 0.22 ng/ml.

Serology for hepatitis B and C viruses, HIV, EBV, CMV, HSV types 1 and 2, Coxiella burnetti and Rickettsias was negative; autoimmunity with ANA, ANCA, rheumatoid factor, immunoglobulins and complements were normal or negative.

Negative Mantoux reaction; Blood cultures through a central catheter, peripheral blood and urine cultures were repeatedly negative; The control cerebrospinal fluid had normal characteristics except for a proteinorrhachia of 65 mg/dl with smear microscopy and culture that were also negative.
The fundus, electrocardiogram, echocardiography and thoraco-abdominal CT with contrast were also normal.

A cranial MRI with contrast was requested, showing a discrete generalized meningeal uptake and multiple lesions measuring between 7-10 mm, hypointense on T1 and hyperintense on T2 and Flair, in the temporal white matter, left external capsule, right periventricular, frontal and bilateral anterior parietal with marked peripheral ring contrast enhancement and associated perilesional edema.

Given the findings compatible with multiple brain abscesses secondary to meningococcemia, an extensive bibliographic search was carried out (clinical practice guidelines, systematic reviews, bibliographic databases, metasearch engines and related non-indexed journals) which confirmed the scarce data reported regarding said complication. .

At this point it was decided to perform a PET-CT with the aim of ruling out other possible findings/foci that would justify the persistence of the febrile condition, corroborating the hypermetabolic uptake of the brain lesions described, and absence of uptake at another body level. .

Ruling out another infectious/inflammatory focus, treatment with parenteral ceftriaxone was continued for 8 weeks, with slow but progressive disappearance of fever, gradual decrease until normalization of CRP and ESR, as well as disappearance of brain abscesses in MRI control after completing treatment. , without presenting complications or recurrence of the condition in the subsequent outpatient follow-up.
